content:
maya: heads-up — after flipping the flag to enable FlashAttention v3 on dedicated, we're seeing a p95 regression on our short-sequence conversational benchmark (128 token cap). canaries show ~15-25% slower p95 compared to v2 for the same model variant. anyone else hit this?

tony: yeah i noticed higher tail on nightly too. looks much worse for multi-turn where kv-cache hits are frequent. not as bad on long-single-shot.

kevin: can you paste the profiler snippet or perf numbers? also which kernel selector settings were used (autoselect vs explicit)?

maya: pasted the minimal repro and profiler output below:
```
bench: conv-shortseq-128
model: rwd-ggml-7b-ql8
flag: flashattn_kernel=v3 (autoselect=true)
metrics: p50=12ms p95=48ms p99=82ms
baseline (v2): p50=11ms p95=40ms p99=78ms
perf traces: increased kernel-switch overhead + ~4ms extra per-token on kv cache hits
stack: attention::flashv3::kernel_dispatch -> kv_cache::lookup -> kernel_dispatch (loop)
```

sasha: interesting — that loop indicates more frequent host<->device handoffs when v3 path hits the paged attention fallback. do we have counts of paged vs fused calls?

maya: not yet. i can add telemetry. initial logs show paged_fallback_rate ~12% when sequence lengths bounce and kv eviction occurs.

riya: could be cache fragmentation + v3 kernel not optimized for small contiguous kv buffers. two quick mitigations: 1) lower flashattn_v3 rollout % and set selector to prefer v2 for shortseq routes; 2) tweak batching heuristic to prefer larger batches (amortize kernel setup).

kevin: +1 to conservative selector. we should gate v3 behind a feature flag with explicit shortseq rule: if seq_len <= 128 && kv_hit_rate > 60% -> prefer v2. easy to add as selector override.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: feature-flag-update: flashattn_v3_enabled=false for pool:dedsim-q1 by @maya at 3500001360

tony: for telemetry, capture: kernel_choice, paged_fallback, kv_buffer_size, kv_eviction_count, input_seq_len, batch_size. add p50/p95 per bucket.

maya: i'll add those metrics and roll flag back on canary while we collect data. question: do we have a safe canary plan for v3 -> v2 fallback that doesn't require per-request retries?

kevin: implement selector with deterministic mapping: per-route override in router layer. that avoids runtime retries. fallback path only triggers on resource OOMs.

riya: also run a microbenchmark that simulates high kv-hit rate with small batches + short seqs; this reproduces the ~15% tail in local runs. i pushed a test to perf repo: perf/flashv3/shortseq_kv_highhit.py

maya: noted. timeline: (1) add telemetry (today), (2) patch selector rule + deploy as a 5% canary (tomorrow), (3) run perf sweep and check p95 delta, (4) decide on wider roll. sound good?

sasha: sounds good. add a regression alert on p95 delta >8% for shortseq routes so we auto-pause.

kevin: one more ask — check quantization path differences. v3 kernel uses a different kernel layout for q8 which might change memory alignment and therefore kv layout. worth profiling memory copy counts.

maya: will capture memcpy counters too. thanks all, i'll post the telemetry link when available. :thumbsup:
